body: There are natural and human causes of climate change.
attribution_text: A geography lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Natural causes of climate change include orbital changes, asteroid collisions, volcanic activity and solar output.
attribution_text: A geography lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Human causes of climate change include the use of fossil fuels, agriculture and deforestation.
attribution_text: A geography lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Human causes of climate change produce greenhouse gases, enhancing the greenhouse effect and leading to global warming.
attribution_text: A geography lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: Milankovitch cycles
body: natural changes in Earth's orbit and tilt over thousands of years that influence solar energy and Earth’s climate
attribution_text: A geography lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: greenhouse gas
body: a gas that contributes to global warming by reducing the amount of radiation leaving Earth’s atmosphere
attribution_text: A geography lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: enhanced greenhouse effect
body: the increased concentration of greenhouse gases in the atmosphere due to human activities, leading to global warming
attribution_text: A geography lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: Climate change is only caused by human activity.
body: Human activity has been significant in recent climate change, but natural factors have caused changes to the climate over millions of years.
attribution_text: A geography lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Climate change due to human activity is causing sea level rise, declining Arctic ice and more extreme weather events.
attribution_text: A geography lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Climate change is affecting people and the environment.
attribution_text: A geography lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: With a range of projections, for example for global temperatures, there is uncertainty about future climates.
attribution_text: A geography lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: extreme weather
body: when a weather event is significantly different from the average or usual weather pattern
attribution_text: A geography lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: social impact
body: the effect on people and communities due to an event or situation
attribution_text: A geography lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: biodiversity
body: the variety of species found in a habitat
attribution_text: A geography lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: food security
body: when people lack secure access to sufficient amounts of safe and nutritious food for normal growth and development and an active and healthy life
attribution_text: A geography lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: All regions will be equally affected by climate change.
body: Different regions experience the effects of climate change differently due to environmental, economic and social factors.
attribution_text: A geography lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Managing climate change can involve mitigation strategies.
attribution_text: A geography lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Mitigation strategies include alternative energy production, carbon capture and planting trees.
attribution_text: A geography lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Mitigation can involve international agreements.
attribution_text: A geography lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: mitigation
body: actions to reduce or prevent the emission of greenhouse gases
attribution_text: A geography lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: renewable energy
body: energy from natural sources that are constantly replenished, like wind and solar
attribution_text: A geography lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: Paris Agreement
body: an international treaty on climate change aiming to limit global warming
attribution_text: A geography lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: Individuals cannot make significant contributions to mitigation.
body: Although national and international mitigation strategies are essential to achieve meaingful mitigation of climate change, individual actions, such as reducing energy use, collectively contribute to mitigation efforts.
attribution_text: A geography lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Managing climate change can involve adaptation strategies.
attribution_text: A geography lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Adaptation strategies include change in agricultural systems and managing water supply.
attribution_text: A geography lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Adaptation involves reducing risk from rising sea levels.
attribution_text: A geography lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: irrigation
body: a method of supplying water to crops to help them grow
attribution_text: A geography lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: desalination
body: the process of removing salt from seawater to make it suitable for drinking and irrigation
attribution_text: A geography lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: coastal defences
body: structures built to protect land from the sea, e.g. sea walls
attribution_text: A geography lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: All adaptation strategies are expensive and complex.
body: Some adaptation strategies are cost-effective and simple, such as rainwater harvesting and crop rotation.
attribution_text: A geography lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

attribution_text: A geography lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

attribution_text: A geography lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

attribution_text: A geography lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: Glacial landforms are not created by climate change.
body: Glacial landforms are often linked to climate change. In many areas we can only see glacial landforms because the ice sheets and glaciers which created them have melted. Climate change also causes glacial processes which modify the landscape.

body: There are global variations in economic development and quality of life.

attribution_text: A geography lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

attribution_text: A geography lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Renewable energy comes from natural processes that are constantly renewed, so they never run out. Recyclable energy comes from resources that are often finite (they can run out) but which can be reprocessed or reused to extend their use.

title: Pupils may think there can only be one legend about Boudica.
body: There are many legends about Boudica's death. Historians from the past have told different stories but we do not know which is the truth.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Constantine was the son of a king in a part of Scotland called Alba.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: When he was very young, his father was killed by someone who wanted to rule in his place.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Constantine had to flee to Ireland where he lived with his aunt who was married to an Irish king.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Constantine was educated at a nearby monastery and as he grew older he planned his revenge.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Eventually Constantine returned to Scotland and defeated his father's enemy at a huge hillfort called Dundurn.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: Alba
body: Alba is the Gaelic name for Scotland and is where southern and central Scotland is today
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: exile
body: someone who is not allowed to live in their own country lives in exile
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: revenge
body: revenge is the act of getting back at someone for something they did to you
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: hillfort
body: a Celtic hillfort was built on top of a hill and surrounded by wooden fences for protection
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: Pupils may think revenge always involves killing people.
body: Revenge is the act of getting back at someone for something they did to you. This may involve stealing something or destroying something like property.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: After he defeated his father's enemy, Constantine became King of Alba, but he had no time to relax.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: His kingdom was under attack by the Vikings, who had taken control of an important place called Dunkeld.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: The bones of an important Scottish saint, Saint Columba, were held there, and the Vikings had taken them.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Constantine led his army against the Vikings, driving them out and recapturing Dunkeld and the relics.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: relics
body: relics are items of religious importance from the past, and are often the remains of saints
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: monastery
body: a monastery is a building where monks live and work together dedicated to religious life
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: Pupils may think the relics of St Columba were valuable.
body: The relics of St Columba were an important symbol of the Christian faith throughout the kingdom of Alba.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: With the Vikings defeated, Constantine now set about strenghtening his kingdom of Alba.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: He changed the Church to make it more like the one he had experienced in Ireland.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: He created a system of mormaers, local leaders who could help him rule over his lands.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Eventually he came into conflict with a powerful king from England and they fought a big battle.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Although Constantine lost, it stopped the king from England from taking control of parts of Scotland.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: Church
body: the Church is the organisation of the Christian religion
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: mormaer
body: a mormaer was a Scottish leader and landowner who helped the king to rule
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: Pupils may think that Athelstan controlled Scotland because he defeated Constantine.
body: Although Constantine lost, Athelstan only remained king of England. He became overlord of Scotland but failed to unite England and Scotland under one kingship.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: John was the youngest son of Henry II and Eleanor of Aquitaine, the King and Queen of England.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: When Henry II died, John's older brother Richard became the King of England.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Richard I was called the 'Lionheart' because he was a brave warrior who was often away from England fighting.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: One time, when Richard I was fighting on a crusade, John began to rule the country as if he was the king.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: This made Richard I angry, and John was exiled for two years; but returned to be named Richard's heir.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: heir
body: a person who expects to inherit the property or position of another when that person dies
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: crusade
body: a crusade was a war fought between different religious groups
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: exiled
body: if someone is exiled, they are forced to leave a place and cannot return
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: Some may think that John's sisters would be in line to the throne before him.
body: Explain that this is the case today in the UK - Princess Charlotte became the first female royal to benefit from The Succession to the Crown Act in 2013. The Act stated that girls born into the Royal Family will not be overtaken by younger brothers.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: In 1199, Richard died during a siege in France and John became the King of England.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: However, John was not a successful king.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: He lost control of lots of English land in France and made his barons pay very high taxes.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: He also argued with the leaders of the Church.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: His actions made his barons very angry with him.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: siege
body: a siege is when an army surrounds a castle or a city to force the people inside to surrender
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: barons
body: the barons were powerful and rich people who owned land and armies in England
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: taxes
body: everyone has to pay money called taxes to the people in charge of a country
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: Church
body: the Church is the organisation of the Christian religion
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: Some may think that the Church is the same as a church building.
body: The Church is the name of the organisation that includes all the people who lead the Christian religion. Buildings are also called churches.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Some of John's barons were so angry with him that they started a rebellion.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: To stop the fighting, John was forced to accept an agreement called Magna Carta.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: In this agreement, John promised not to tax his barons so heavily, and to behave better in the future.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Magna Carta made John weaker and his barons stronger.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Even after John died, kings and queens that followed him have followed the agreements set out in Magna Carta.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: rebellion
body: a rebellion is an act of armed resistance against a government or leader
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: Magna Carta
body: Magna Carta was a written document that set out the rules a king or queen had to follow
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: laws
body: laws are a set of rules that everyone has to follow
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: Some may think that kings and queens after King John forgot about Magna Carta.
body: Kings and queens after King John still followed Magna Carta and it remained as a very important document of rights for the people. Today, there are still four of the original 63 clauses in use in England.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Suleiman was born in a place called the Ottoman Empire, which controlled lots of land in Europe and the Middle East.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Suleiman's father was the Sultan of the Ottoman Empire, and when he died in 1520, Suleiman became the new Sultan.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Suleiman wanted to make his empire stronger by fighting wars and conquering land.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: He conquered places all over Europe, North Africa and the Middle East.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: He even reached as far as the grand city of Vienna, but had to turn back because his army ran out of supplies.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: Ottoman Empire
body: the Ottoman Empire ruled over large areas of the Middle East and Eastern Europe for over 600 years
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: Sultan
body: the leader of the Ottoman Empire was known as the Sultan
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: siege
body: a siege is when an army surrounds a castle or a city to force the people inside to surrender
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: Vienna
body: Vienna is the capital city of Austria, a country in Europe
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: Some may think that the failure to capture Vienna meant Suleiman was a failure.
body: Emphasise that setbacks are normal and Suleiman was still able to extend the Ottoman Empire to its greatest ever reach.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Suleiman was not just a powerful general; he cared about the law and making sure his empire was run fairly.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Suleiman changed the laws in the Ottoman Empire so that everyone followed the same rules.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: He also spent lots of money improving the cities of his empire.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: In major Islamic cities like Mecca, Damascus and Baghdad he built great mosques, bridges and even aqueducts.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: He spent huge sums of money building an impressive mosque in Istanbul that is named after him.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: laws
body: laws are a set of rules that everyone has to follow
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: mosque
body: a mosque is a Muslim place of worship
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: aqueduct
body: an aqueduct was a series of bridges used to transport clean drinking water to towns
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: Mecca
body: Mecca is the most important city in the religion of Islam and many choose to make a long journey to travel there
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: Some may think that the buildings commissioned by Suleiman are not used or in existence today.
body: Many of them still exist 500 years later and can be seen today, particularly the mosques and religious buildings which have been continually renovated over time.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Suleiman loved art, poetry and literature, even composing poems himself.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: He spent huge amounts of money making his palace a centre for art and writing.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Artists, poets and writers from all over the Ottoman Empire were paid to paint and write for him.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: With all these beautiful paintings and wonderful pieces of writing, this time has been called a 'Golden Age'.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: In the West, people have given Suleiman the nickname, 'the Magnificent' because of this.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: Golden Age
body: a Golden Age is a time of peace, prosperity and plenty
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: literature
body: literature is writing that is thought of as a work of art
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: Some may think that 'Suleiman the Lawgiver' and 'Suleiman the Magnificent' are different people.
body: Explain that these are different names used for the same person to remember different elements of his time as Sultan of the Ottoman Empire.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Eleanor of Aquitaine was the daughter of the Duke of Aquitaine, an important landholder in what is modern France.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Her father made sure that she received a good education and she was taught about literature, languages and how to ride!
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Her father expected her to marry a duke, prince or king, and this education would be very useful.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: However, before he could see her married, the Duke of Aquitaine died, leaving Eleanor all of his lands.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Just 13 years old, Eleanor was now the rich and powerful Duchess of Aquitaine.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: Aquitaine
body: Aquitaine was a large area of modern day France. The person who controlled it was known as the Duke or Duchess of Aquitaine
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: inherit
body: to receive money, property or possessions from someone after the person has died
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: Some may think that Aquitaine is the same as modern day France.
body: Aquitaine was only one area of modern day France, there were lots of areas controlled by different powerful families at this time.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Shortly after her father's death, Eleanor married a French prince, Louis.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Even though Louis became the Duke of Aquitaine, Eleanor got to keep her land for herself.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Louis became King of France shortly after their marriage, and Eleanor helped him to rule.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Eleanor went with Louis on a crusade, travelling to Constantinople and Jerusalem.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Eleanor and Louis' marriage broke down and it was annulled, leaving her free to marry again.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: crusade
body: a crusade was a war fought between different religious groups
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: annulled
body: when a marriage is annulled, it means that the two people are officially no longer married
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: Some may think that Eleanor and Louis were not married for very long.
body: Eleanor and Louis were married for 15 years before their marriage was annulled by the church.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Two months after her marriage to Louis was annulled, Eleanor married Henry, who was next in line to the English throne.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Henry became the King of England, and Eleanor was his queen; together they ruled over large parts of France and England.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: However, their marriage was not always happy and eventually Eleanor moved back to Aquitaine.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: When her sons decided to revolt against Henry, she supported them and Henry had her confined as punishment.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: However, after Henry's death she helped two of her sons, Richard and John, to rule when they were king of England.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: rebel
body: to rebel means to go against a leader
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: prisoner
body: when someone is a prisoner they are kept in one place and do not have the freedom to leave
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: Some may think of Eleanor as a prisoner being kept in terrible conditions.
body: Eleanor lived in places of comfort, for example, castles. She did not have the freedom to leave but was well looked after.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Musa Keita was an important man living in the large and powerful empire of Mali.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: The mansa of Mali wanted to explore beyond the seas, and set off on a voyage into the Atlantic Ocean.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: He gave the instruction that if he did not return, Musa Keita should become the mansa.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: He never returned, and Musa became Mansa Musa, emperor of Mali.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Mansa Musa used Mali's army to conquer lands rich with gold, making Mali even more powerful and wealthy.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: empire
body: an empire is a group of countries or provinces ruled from the centre by a person or group of people
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: mansa
body: all rulers of the Mali Empire were called mansas
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: conquer
body: to conquer means to take control of another place
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: wealthy
body: If you have a lot of money and own many expensive things then you are wealthy
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: Pupils may think Musa Keita was meant to be mansa.
body: Musa Keita became mansa because the previous mansa did not return from his voyage and he chose Musa Keita to replace him.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Mansa Musa was a Muslim and his faith was very strong.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: He knew that as a Muslim, he should travel to the holy city of Mecca on a pilgrimage called the Hajj.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: He made the long journey to Mecca accompanied by many people and camels, carrying huge amounts of gold.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: During the journey Mansa Musa gave this gold away to the people that he met.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: His journey and the gold made Mansa Musa and Mali famous throughout the Islamic world.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: pilgrimage
body: a pilgrimage is a journey to a holy place
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: Hajj
body: Hajj is the name for the Muslim pilgrimage
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: Islamic
body: Islamic means relating to Islam
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: Pupils may think all Muslims have to do the pilgrimage.
body: The pilgrimage is something many Muslims would like to do. However, it is only required if they are able to do it. Travelling to Mecca is too expensive for many people. Others might not be physically able to do the pilgrimage.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: When Mansa Musa returned from the Hajj he spent time in one of the cities that his generals had conquered.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: This city was Timbuktu, and Mansa Musa ordered great mosques to be built there to spread Islam.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Under Mansa Musa's rule, Timbuktu became very important for trade, with desert caravans linking it to North Africa.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: It also became a place of learning and education with one of the mosques made into a place for teaching.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Scholars travelled from all over the Islamic world to learn about history, Islam and law.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: mosque
body: a mosque is a Muslim place of worship
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: Islam
body: Islam is the religion followed by Muslims, who believe that there is one God: Allah
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: caravan
body: a caravan is group of people travelling together on camels, usually to sell things
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: scholar
body: a scholar is someone who spends a lot of time studying and learning; they often become experts in their chosen areas and share what they learn with others
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: Pupils may confuse the term caravan.
body: Explain to pupils that a group of camels is called a caravan.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: At the age of 21, a young woman called Elizabeth found herself imprisoned in the Tower of London.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: She had been accused of plotting to take the throne by her older half-sister Mary, who was queen.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: It was very likely that Mary might order her to be executed, so Elizabeth wrote her a letter saying she was innocent.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Although Mary refused to see Elizabeth, she eventually freed her and Elizabeth's life was spared.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Soon after, Mary died and Elizabeth became Queen of England.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: executed
body: executed means someone being killed as a legal punishment
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: Plotting
body: Plotting is when, in secret, you plan to do something bad.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: Tower of London
body: the Tower of London is a building used to defend the King or Queen
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: Pupils may think Elizabeth had a right to the throne when her father Henry VIII died.
body: At this time, the heir to the throne was the first-born son of the King rather than the first-born child.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: As queen, Elizabeth I had lots of problems.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: England had a powerful enemy, Spain, and arguments over religion had torn the country apart.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Elizabeth's advisors wanted her to have children quickly so that if she died, her children could take over from her.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: However, Elizabeth was more concerned with solving England's problems, and never married or had children.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: This has led her to be remembered as a queen who put her country before herself.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: government
body: a government is a group of leaders who make laws and decisions for a country
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: debt
body: a debt is something, especially money, that is owed to someone else
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: religion
body: a religion is a set of beliefs and practices
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: Pupils may think all kings and queens needed to be married.
body: Elizabeth decided she didn’t want to marry and she proved that she didn’t need to be to be a successful queen.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Elizabeth I faced one of her greatest challenges in 1588 when mighty Spain went to war with England.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Spain wanted to invade England and take control of it, so they sent a huge armada to do so.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Elizabeth sent her best sailors to fight the Spanish in the English Channel to stop them from invading.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: At the same time, Elizabeth made a famous speech to her army at Tilbury, saying she was as brave as any king.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Although the English had fewer ships, they were helped by the weather, which blew the Spanish ships away from England.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: armada
body: an armada was a large group of warships

body: Mehr al-Nesā was born in Kandahar, part of the mighty Mughal Empire in what is now Afghanistan.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Her name meant 'sun among women', but she would later have a new name, Nūr Jahān.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Her parents were running away from another country where they had been treated badly.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: A story is told about Mehr al-Nesā during this time; that on their journey her parents abandoned her in the desert.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Feeling awful about what they had done, they returned to find their daughter sitting calmly next to a dangerous snake.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: Mughal Empire

attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: Pupils may think Mehr al-Nesā sitting next to a snake is completely true.
body: Explain to the pupils that Mehr al-Nesā's early life is still unknown. There are only legends about her story. A legend is a traditional story that might not always be true.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Growing up in India, Mehr al-Nesā married a Mughal official and together they had a baby daughter.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: However, her husband was killed after an argument with the local governor, and Mehr al-Nesā became a widow.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: At this time, widows were welcomed to the Mughal Emperor's court to keep his wives company.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: The emperor, Jahāngīr, had nineteen wives; when he saw Mehr al-Nesā he fell in love with her straight away.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: They married and she was given a new title, Nūr Jahān (Light of the World), and became his favourite wife.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: an official is someone who works for someone important like the Mughal Emperor
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: Pupils may be confused by the emperor having 20 wives.
body: Explain to pupils that in some countries and some religions you can marry multiple people. However today in the UK, it is illegal to marry more than one person.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Jahāngīr was quite a sick man and described how Nūr Jahān was better than any doctor at making him feel better.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Jahāngīr also wrote about how Nūr Jahān was a skilful hunter, managing to shoot a lion whilst sitting on an elephant.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Jahāngīr was not a strong ruler, and gave Nūr Jahān his imperial seal, making her the true ruler of Mughal India.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: This made her very powerful and she even minted her own coins and issued royal orders that everyone had to follow.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: During the last years of Jahāngīr's life she used her power to build a huge white marble tomb for her father.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: Pupils may think Emperor Jahāngīr was angry with Nūr Jahān for becoming powerful.
body: Explain to pupils that Emperor Jahāngīr admired Nūr Jahān and was grateful to her for looking after him and taking care of his responsibilities while he was ill.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: St. Patrick was born in Britain when it was controlled by a group of people called the Romans.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: He grew up in a Christian family but did not believe in God as a child.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Aged 16, he was captured by Irish raiders and taken as an enslaved person to Ireland for 6 years.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: During his captivity, he worked as a shepherd and during this time his belief in God got stronger.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: One day, he had a dream telling him that he would soon go home, so he fled to the coast and sailed back to Britain.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: Christian
body: someone who follows the Christian religion, believing in God and Jesus, is described as a Christian
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: Romans
body: the Romans were a group of people from Italy that took over lots of land across Europe, Africa and the Middle East
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: raider
body: a raider is someone who attacks people or places by surprise, often to steal from them
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: shepherd
body: someone who herds and looks after sheep is called a shepherd
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: That St. Patrick was Irish.
body: Explain to children that St. Patrick was born in Britain. As a teenager, he was captured by raiders and taken to Ireland.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Having returned to Britain, St. Patrick had a vision which convinced him to return to Ireland.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: When he reached Ireland, he travelled around teaching people about Christianity.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: One popular story about St. Patrick is how he used the shamrock to explain some important things about Christianity.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: The shamrock has since become one of the symbols of Ireland.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Another popular story about St. Patrick was that he drove all of the snakes out of Ireland, chasing them into the sea.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: vision
body: when people have an imagined experience it is known as a vision
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: missionary
body: a missionary is a person sent on a religious mission, especially to promote Christianity in foreign countries
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: shamrock
body: a clover plant with three leaves is called a shamrock
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: That snakes used to live in Ireland.
body: Explain that snakes were unlikely to have ever lived in Ireland due to the geography and climate. It is thought that the snakes in the story of St. Patrick and the snakes of Ireland were a metaphor or symbol.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Aethelflaed was the daughter of Alfred, a king of a place in Britain called Wessex.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Aethelflaed lived in Britain at a time when her people, the Anglo-Saxons, were under attack from the Vikings.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: The Vikings had travelled across the sea to settle in Britain, and they were willing to fight for their new lands.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: As Aethelflaed grew up, the Vikings took more and more land, almost capturing Alfred and his family.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: When Aethelflaed was around the age of 16, her father Alfred won a big victory against the Vikings and made peace.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: Anglo-Saxons
body: the Anglo-Saxons were the people who lived in Britain at the time of Aethelflaed and Alfred
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: court
body: playing area where a game or sport is played
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: Vikings
body: the Vikings were raiders from Scandinavia who attacked and settled in Britain at the time of Aethelflaed and Alfred
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: victory
body: when someone or a group of people win something it is called a victory
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: The Anglo-Saxons only had one king in Britain.
body: The Anglo-Saxons had different kingdoms in Britain, each with its own king.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Alfred needed other parts of Britain to be strong again, so he arranged for Aethelflaed to marry the leader of Mercia.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: The man Aethelflaed married was called Aethelred, and together they made Mercia strong again to resist the Vikings.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Aethelred was much older than Aethelflaed; as he got old and sick and eventually died, Aethelflaed ruled Mercia herself.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Aethelflaed stood up to the Vikings; ordering a group of soldiers to go on a special mission into Viking lands.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: The soldiers brought back the bones of an important Anglo-Saxon saint, Oswald, which won Aethelflaed a lot of respect.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: Mercia
body: Mercia was a major Anglo-Saxon kingdom in the central part of England
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: respect
body: showing consideration for other people's feelings, opinions and beliefs
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: saint
body: a saint is a holy person who has died and been officially recognised and honoured by the Christian church
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: The names Aethelflaed and Aethelred are very similar and may be mistaken for the same person.
body: Highlight that the two names are very similar but that Aethelflaed was the daughter of Alfred the Great and became Lady of Mercia, whereas Aethelred was the king of the Anglo-Saxon kingdom of Mercia.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Owain Glyndwr was a Welshman who was born at a time when England controlled Wales.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: He was descended from the princes of a part of Wales.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: As a young man he travelled to London to study law and even fought in an English army.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: When he returned to Wales, he found that many people were unhappy with English rule.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Owain Glyndwr decided to fight to try and make Wales free from English rule.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: Marches
body: the Marches is a place between Wales and England
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: lord

attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: That life was the same 750 years ago as it is today.
body: Explain to children that lots of things were very different 750 years ago. For example, there were no cars, planes or trains and it would have taken Owain a long time to travel to Scotland and London. People would have travelled by horse or walked.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Gaining support from many people in Wales, Owain and his forces captured many castles including Conwy castle.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: After a few years, Owain and his army had gained control of most of Wales.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Owain pronounced himself the Prince of Wales, a title that English kings had given to their heirs.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: However, the English fought back and, after a few years, most of Wales was back under its control.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Owain refused to surrender, now and again ambushing English soldiers who never managed to capture him.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: an act of resistance or rebellion
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: The Welsh lords were chanting 'Owain Glyndwr, Prince of Wales' because he was the Prince.
body: Ensure children know that the Welsh lords were chanting because they wanted Owain to become the Prince of Wales and their leader.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: At the time of Robert the Bruce, England and Scotland were separate countries.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: The English king, Edward I, invaded Scotland because he wanted them to do what he said.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Robert the Bruce was a young Scottish noble who decided to stand up to the English King.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: He became King of Scotland and this made Edward very angry.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Robert was forced to run away; his family were captured and put in prison.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: invade
body: when a group of people attack another country, moving their soldiers into it, they invade that country
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: Robert the Bruce is a fictional character in a story.
body: Ensure that children understand that Robert the Bruce was a real person from the past.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: One of the most famous legends told about Robert the Bruce is the story of him and a spider.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: While Robert was hiding from the English, it was said that he sheltered from the Scottish winter in a cave.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: In this cave, Robert watched a spider again and again try to spin its web; every time it fell it tried again.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: This made Robert realise that he had to keep trying against the English.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Inspired by the spider, Robert returned to Scotland and eventually forced the English out of his homeland.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: That legends are true.
body: Ensure children understand that legends are stories that are often told verbally and may change over time. Play a game to demonstrate this; children sit in a circle and pass a message around by whispering to each other. Does the messgae change?

body: Almost 200 years ago, a woman called Victoria became the Queen of the United Kingdom.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: She would go on to rule for longer than any other monarch before her and be remembered as very important.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: However, when she was very little her life was very sad, later Victoria would describe it as 'melancholy'.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: She was very lonely; her father died when she was just one year old and her mother was very protective of her.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Victoria did not meet many other children, spending her days learning or playing with her dolls and her dog, Dash.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: monarch
body: a sovereign head of state, such as a king, queen or emperor
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: melancholy
body: feeling or expressing a deep sadness
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: That nothing is known about Victoria (or indeed other monarchs) before becoming Queen.
body: There is a lot of historical evidence about Victoria's childhood including written accounts and artefacts that tell us a great deal about what her early life was like.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: In 1837, Victoria became queen when she was 18 years old.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Victoria was very popular when she became queen; 400,000 people visited London for her coronation in 1838.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: She had little experience of how to rule the country and relied on her prime minister, who led the government, for help.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: coronation
body: a coronation is an official ceremony where a king or a queen receives their crown
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: Prime Minister
body: the leader of the political party who is in power and head of the government
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: government
body: a government is a group of leaders who make laws and decisions for a country
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: law
body: a law is a rule that tells people what they can and cannot do
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: That a coronation ceremony is when a person becomes a monarch.
body: The person who is first in line to the throne becomes monarch the minute that the previous monarch passes away. It happens in an instant. The coronation is an official ceremony, held later where the monarch receives their crown in front of people.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Before Victoria became queen she had met her cousin Albert several times, and described him as 'handsome'.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Although she did not marry him straight away, once Victoria was queen she proposed to Albert.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Victoria and Albert were in love from the early days of their marriage.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: On their wedding day in 1840, Victoria wrote in her diary that 'This was the happiest day of my life!'
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: cousin
body: people with different parents but the same grandparents are cousins
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: handsome
body: something or someone that has a pleasing and healthy appearance can be described as handsome
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: marry
body: when two people marry, they promise to spend their life together, in a ceremony that is watched by other people
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: propose
body: when someone asks someone else to marry them they propose
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: That Victoria and Albert only married because they were made to do so, not because they loved each other.
body: Victoria and Albert had a strong connection from the first time they met. Written evidence tells us that the two were very much in love and their marriage was a happy, loving relationship.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Victoria wrote about her pregnancies in her diaries: she didn't like being pregnant and wrote newborn babies were ugly.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Victoria and Albert's first child, a girl they named Victoria, was born in November 1840.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Victoria and Albert had nine children together; her first son, Albert Edward, became king when Queen Victoria died.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: When her 8th and 9th babies were born, Queen Victoria used special new medical invention called chloroform.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Thanks to Victoria, chloroform became quite popular, which helped many other women when they were having babies.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: diaries
body: when people write about their life they sometimes write in books called diaries
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: pregnant
body: when a woman is pregnant she is going to give birth to a baby
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: chloroform
body: chloroform was used in Victorian England to reduce pain
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: That inventions are always things like machines, robots, computers and so on.
body: Inventions come from ideas, and people can have ideas about so many different situations in life. The invention here for example is a type of pain relief for childbirth, a medical invention.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: During Victoria's reign there were very clear groups of people, called classes, in society.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Ford Madox Brown's 1865 painting called 'Work' shows some of these alongside many other aspects of Victorian life.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: In the middle of the painting are a group of workers called 'navvies', who are digging up the road to build a tunnel.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Around them are both rich and poor men and women, a group of orphaned children and some sleeping unemployed men.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: At the top of the painting are two wealthy figures on horseback whose progress has been stopped by the work.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: society
body: a society is a large group of people who live within the same area and usually share similar cultures and beliefs
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: classes
body: classes are groups of people based on the job they do or how much money they have
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: wealthy
body: If you have a lot of money and own many expensive things then you are wealthy

title: Pupils may think that classes in society are small groups, like classes at school.
body: Classes are groups of people, but classes in society include thousands, sometimes millions of people and they are not age related like school classes, they depend on other factors like wealth or profession.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: During Victorian times, Britain changed a lot as people left the countryside to work in new factories in towns.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Some people thought these changes were good; this can be seen in William Wyld's painting 'Manchester from Kersal Moor'.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: He makes the factory chimneys look pretty by putting them next to church spires, and painting golden sunlight on them.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: But these cities and towns were not nice places to live, with lots of crowding, pollution and poor health.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: These poor conditions can be seen in Gustave Doré's engraving 'Over London - By Rail'.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: factories
body: factories are large buildings in which different goods are made
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: chimney
body: chimneys extend out of the roof of a building, they carry smoke from a fire inside the building and allow it to be released into the sky
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: spire
body: a spire is a tall, narrow, pointed structure usually on top of a church tower
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: Pupils may think that only adults worked at jobs in factories in Victorian times.
body: In Victorian times, there were no laws stopping children working. Children had to earn money to live, so many of them worked in factories. Since they were young and small, children were useful for getting into tight spaces to clean or fix machines.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Many people in Victorian Britain were proud of new inventions that were introduced at that time.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Prince Albert was one of these people; in 1851, he organised the Great Exhibition to celebrate new modern inventions.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: The Crystal Palace, a huge steel and glass building, was built for the exhibition.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Albert invited inventors from all over Britain and the world to show off their inventions.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: More than six million people, roughly a third of Britain's population, visited the exhibition.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: invention
body: an invention is something new that has never been created before
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: modern
body: something to do with the present or current time is described as modern
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: exhibition
body: an exhibition is a public show of art, crafts, products, or skills
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

title: Pupils may think that the Crystal Palace is still standing or that it can be seen or visited today.
body: The Crystal Palace was a temporary structure built for the exhibition. It was relocated and rebuilt in another part of London but was later destroyed by fire. The surrounding area was then named Crystal Palace to show how important the structure was.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: When Victoria became queen, she ruled England, Scotland, Wales and Ireland.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: In 1842, she was meant to go on holiday in Europe, but became ill so her advisers arranged for her to visit Scotland.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: Both she and Albert fell in love with Scotland, buying an estate at Balmoral and building their own castle there.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)

body: When Albert died in 1861, Victoria was very sad. She was comforted by John Brown, a Scottish servant at Balmoral.
attribution_text: A history lesson by Oak National Academy licensed under Open Government Licence (OGL)
